# `Browser.Channel`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Browser.Channel — a session-stream for cross-tab message exchange over
the `BroadcastChannel` API, via `Ipe.Ffi.Js` ports.

A first-party proof of the per-capability web mechanism spanning BOTH port
directions: outbound `JsCmd` frames open a named channel, send typed message
payloads, and close it; inbound `JsMsg` frames carry received message payloads
or typed error variants. Both cross the same seal codec and fail-closed port
discipline as every other port; there is no second transport.

Importing this reserved `Ipe.Browser.<Api>` module discloses
`js-port:channel` (import-derived, keyed on the canonical `Ipe.Browser.Channel`
path prefix via `WebCapability::for_browser_module`, alias-immune); only the
top-level app's `[capabilities] accepts` set can grant it.

The two layers:

  * `Ipe.Browser.Channel.Internals` publishes the closed outbound/inbound ADTs.
  * this module is the high-level layer: `open` starts the channel session as
    an outbound `Cmd`, `send` posts a message, `close` tears it down, and
    `messages` is the inbound subscription folding the narrow `JsMsg` into a
    typed `ChannelEvent`. The inbound `case` is EXHAUSTIVE: an unavailability
    becomes a typed variant, never a silently dropped frame.

## `ChannelEvent`

A typed channel event delivered by the message subscription.

  * `ChannelMessage payload` — a message received on the named channel from
    another tab or worker. `payload` is the string content of the message.
  * `ChannelUnavailable` — the `BroadcastChannel` API is absent in this
    browser context.

## `open`

```ipe
open : String -> Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`open name` — open a `BroadcastChannel` with the given name. Future
messages posted to the same channel name (from this tab or others) arrive
on the `messages` subscription. Outbound `Cmd`.

The channel name is a plain string identifier; the JS host creates a
`new BroadcastChannel(name)`. A missing `BroadcastChannel` API replies
immediately with `Unavailable` rather than silently failing.

Importing this module discloses `js-port:channel`; the app must grant it
with `accepts = [ JsPort Channel ]` under [capabilities] in package.ipe.

## `send`

```ipe
send : String -> String -> Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`send name payload` — post a string message on the named channel. All
subscribers in other tabs or workers sharing that channel name will receive
it. Fire-and-forget; no inbound reply. Outbound `Cmd`.

## `close`

```ipe
close : String -> Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`close name` — close the `BroadcastChannel` with the given name, removing
the event listener. A no-op when no open channel with that name exists.
Outbound `Cmd`.

## `messages`

```ipe
messages : (ChannelEvent -> msg) -> Sub.Sub msg
```

`messages toMsg` — the inbound subscription, wired in `subscriptions`.

The decoder IS the security gate: every inbound value runs through the total,
bounded seal decoder for the narrow `JsMsg`; a malformed / mismatched frame is
dropped whole. A decoded `JsMsg` is folded EXHAUSTIVELY into a `ChannelEvent`.
